— the orqAgent team

brief.arc: Single email. It opens on the launch as news framed in the reader's terms (an agent that answers handbook questions in Slack), makes the case for why it matters to them specifically — the answers already exist, the cost is a person finding them again every time, and the usual fix is a stack they would own forever — then narrows the ask to one agent over one set of policy documents.
brief.sequence_rationale: One email was requested, so the entire argument has to survive being read cold and once. I chose the Slack-plus-your-own-documents pairing over the two obvious alternatives — the analytics/run-log angle and the price angle — for three reasons. Price is table stakes: five competitors publish the same $0/$29 shape, and our own pricing pages disagree with each other, so quoting a number invites the one objection the evidence cannot beat. The analytics angle is genuinely open ground, but it answers a question this reader only asks after the bot exists; it is the better second email, not the first. Slack is where this audience has already decided the bot must live, and E90 is the only evidence describing the bot replying to mentions and channel messages there, so it carries the announcement. The objection assigned — 'Nobody here owns internal tooling — who keeps this running after I build it?' — is the one that actually stops this reader, and it is answerable from evidence. Two objections are deliberately unassigned because the material cannot beat them: the SOC 2 report request (certification is in progress, and no email fixes that) and the pricing-table contradiction (the tables genuinely disagree, which is why the copy states no plan limits at all). Retrieval is keyword scoring over ~500-token chunks, not semantic search, so the email invites a test rather than claiming answer quality. The single thing the user could send us that would most change this campaign: which customers or quotes may we name — there is not one customer name, quote or usage figure in the entire material, so every line is currently the company asserting things about itself.
